title: Turn windows, idea cues, handoff next-steps, and the prompts sidecar (deterministic; no rendered-output change)
plainTerms: This phase teaches honestweek to notice which of your instructions each piece of evidence belongs to. Today it sweeps a coding session into four undifferentiated piles: what you asked for, what the assistant said, whether tests passed, and which commits came up. Nothing links a pile to the instruction that caused it. After this phase it still collects exactly the same things, but each one is also filed under the instruction that came just before it. It also learns to tell your real instructions apart from the notices the tool itself pastes into a session, so a status message never gets treated as something you asked for. It additionally starts noticing two things it ignored before: when you float an idea in passing, and when a session-end note lists work that is still open. Nothing new appears in any report, web page or file you publish. The two visible changes are that the private working file honestweek writes for itself gets richer, and a second private file appears beside it holding the exact wording of your instructions, so the published report never has to carry it. Both private files are added to the ignore list before either is created, so neither can be committed by accident.
requirements: Fix the ordering defect first. At every place lib/claude-adapter.mjs mines a string, redact BEFORE truncate instead of truncate-then-redact. Measured defect: a 303-char string ending 'alice@corp-secret.example.com more' currently emits 'alice@corp-...' because the cut removes the trailing TLD that EMAIL_RE requires. Call sites: claude-adapter.mjs:345 (steers), :347 (redirects), :370/:372 (notes). redact() is idempotent, so the deepRedact backstop at :518 still holds. Do NOT change lib/redact.mjs (test/redact.test.mjs:19 pins its public surface to exactly ['count','deepRedact','redact']). State the real blast radius in the PR body: this shifts the cut for EVERY over-length mined string carrying any redactable token before the cut, not only for a secret straddling the boundary (measured: a 358-char string with '/home/alice/notes' at offset 40 yields 279 chars old order, 281 new).

Create a new pure module lib/lanes.mjs (Node built-ins only, no I/O, no network). It owns: IDEA_CUES, a closed cue vocabulary with one generic regex each — 'what-if' (/\bwhat if\b/i), 'we-could' (/\bwe could\b/i), 'idea' ANCHORED to a line start (/^\s*idea[:,]/im, never a bare occurrence), 'worth-trying' (/\bworth (a )?try(ing)?\b/i). Bare 'later' is DROPPED: it fires constantly in ordinary assistant prose and would let the assistant side dominate the band. Also: shortHash(str) (FNV-1a -> 8 hex, copy handoffs.mjs:40-47); normalizePhrase(str) (lowercase, collapse whitespace, strip punctuation); FILLER, a stopword/filler set ('continue','yes','ok','go ahead','do it','keep going','next','please','thanks', plus articles/pronouns/auxiliaries); shapeKeyFor(text) -> string|null; refFor(sessionId, turnIndex, origin, redactedText) = shortHash of those four joined by '|'; and sharesRun(authored, corpusStrings). All vocabularies must be generic English; no operator, project or client noun.

shapeKeyFor must have a FLOOR and must be able to refuse. Return null when, after normalizePhrase and FILLER removal, fewer than 6 distinct content words remain. Otherwise return shortHash of the first 6 remaining content words with digit runs mapped to '#'. A null shapeKey means the window is ineligible for recurrence and for every Lane A grade. Rationale, measured over 300 real session logs under ~/.claude/projects using the unfloored first-6-words fingerprint: 179 of 662 distinct fingerprints (27%) recurred across 2 or more DISTINCT sessions, and the top recurring ones were 'heads up you are going to' (26 sessions), 'scheduled task name nightly wiki digest' (22), 'local command stdout set model to' (22) and 'local command caveat caveat the messages' (22). None is a technique. Without a floor, CLI plumbing out-competes real instructions for the strongest evidence grade.

sharesRun(authored, corpusStrings) must be LENGTH-ADAPTIVE and must not be inert on short strings. Normalize both sides. Let w = authored word count. Return true if (a) the whole normalized authored string occurs as a substring of any normalized corpus string, at ANY length, or (b) any run of n = min(8, max(3, ceil(0.6 * w))) consecutive authored words occurs in any corpus string. A fixed n = 8 was inert for exactly the strings it guards: technique and forward names are short by construction, so a verbatim 5-, 6- or 7-word lift of the operator's instruction passed unconditionally.

Export a correction predicate from lib/claude-adapter.mjs: `export function isCorrectionTurn(text)` wrapping the existing REDIRECT_RE (:308) and REDIRECT_BODY_RE (:309) verbatim. Do not change the regexes. This exists so a later cross-session pass cannot fork the definition.

Add a CLOSED machine-envelope classifier, not a single prefix. isHumanTurn (claude-adapter.mjs:133-141) rejects only content starting '<command-'. Censused over 300 real session files: 1177 non-command user string turns, whose opening tags include <task-notification> (278), <local-command-caveat> (36), <local-command-stdout> (36), <system-reminder> (17) and <cross-session-message from=... name="..."> (10). Every one passes isHumanTurn. Add `MACHINE_ENVELOPE_TAGS = ['command-name','command-message','command-args','local-command-stdout','local-command-stderr','local-command-caveat','task-notification','system-reminder','scheduled-task','cross-session-message','user-prompt-submit-hook']` and `isMachineEnvelope(text)`: true when the first non-whitespace character is '<' AND the opening tag name is in the set, OR (catch-all) the content consists solely of one or more well-formed <tag ...>...</tag> blocks with no free prose outside them. Unknown tags are treated as machine, not human — the fail-closed direction.

Add a window-boundary predicate `isTurnBoundary(rec)` SEPARATE from isHumanTurn. Do NOT modify isHumanTurn: it also gates probeHead's `interactive` flag (:157), which decides whether a session is emitted at all, and test/claude-adapter.test.mjs:59 pins the entry count at exactly 3. isTurnBoundary(rec) returns true iff rec is a user record with string content that is non-empty AND either (a) not a machine envelope (kind 'prose'), or (b) an envelope whose opening tag is 'command-name' (kind 'command'). Every other envelope class returns FALSE and opens no window. This is the fix for the trap the single-prefix rule created: <local-command-caveat> and <local-command-stdout> appear 36 times each against 36 <command-name> turns, so under the old rule every slash command was immediately followed by two machine records that each opened a fresh window, attributing the command's work to its own stdout. For a command turn the window's instruction text is the <command-name> content ONLY; <command-args> content is never read, never hashed, never written to the sidecar.

Add bounds beside claude-adapter.mjs:50-56: MAX_TURNS = 400, MAX_TOOLS_PER_TURN = 20, MAX_STATUS_PER_TURN = 20, MAX_SHAS_PER_TURN = 10, MAX_IDEAS = 40, MAX_PROMPT_LEN = 4000, MAX_SIDECAR_BYTES = 8388608.

Enumerate EXHAUSTIVELY which caps set a window's `complete` flag to false, because the earlier rule ('every bound that bites while a window is open') made two acceptance criteria mutually unsatisfiable. Caps that DO set complete = false on the open window: MAX_TOOLS_PER_TURN, MAX_STATUS_PER_TURN, MAX_SHAS_PER_TURN, MAX_IDEAS — these are the WINDOW-LOCAL evidence bounds, and their loss is what makes a window ungradeable. Caps that DO NOT touch the flag: MAX_STEERS (52), MAX_NOTES (53), MAX_STATUS (54), MAX_REDIRECTS (55), MAX_CANDIDATES (56) — every one caps a FLAT legacy array the window projection never reads, and the window's own tallies are computed independently. Under the old rule MAX_STEERS biting at the 61st human turn would have marked every later window incomplete, which contradicts the requirement that a 100-turn session still support cross-session recurrence.

Windows past MAX_TURNS become STUBS, not absences. Emit `{ index, stub: true, complete: false }` with no other fields. The earlier rule ('every dropped-past-cap window absent rather than present-and-incomplete') made truncation invisible to any universal quantifier over a shapeKey group, so a corrected use of a technique at turn 450 simply did not exist in the data the 'held up' check ranges over — the inverted-bias trap reappearing at the MAX_TURNS boundary. Also record `truncatedAtTurn: <index>|null` on the session entry.

Segment the record stream into turn windows inside extractEntry (:321). Add `turns: []`, `ideas: []` and an uncapped `counters` object to the acc literal (:322-332). Open a window at the isTurnBoundary branch; flush the open window before `return acc` at :381 (the final window has no closing turn and is usually the most productive one). Each emitted non-stub turn is a PLAIN object with FIXED keys: { index, ref, shapeKey (string|null), kind: 'prose'|'command', opensWithCorrection: boolean, correctionObserved: 'yes'|'no'|'unknown', complete: boolean, stub: false, assistantTurns: number, toolsUsed: object, statusSignals: string[], testSignals: string[], commitShas: string[], inspectedShas: string[] }. `index` is the window's 0-based position in turns[] and is the value a receipt's `turn` must equal. No Set, no Map, no mined text as an object key — deepRedact collapses Set/Map to {} silently (measured) and never redacts KEYS (redact.mjs:217, measured: deepRedact({'Falcon-technique':3}) returns the codename intact).

`toolsUsed` is a COUNTS OBJECT ({ Edit: 2, Bash: 1 }), never a string array. lib/harvest.mjs collectStrings walks Object.values() recursively and never collects KEYS, so tool names stay invisible to the denylist proposer exactly as they are today under toolSignal.counts. Measured: harvestNouns returns a candidate for each of 'Edit','Bash','Grep','Read','Write','Glob','Task' (all match isCandidate's /^[A-Z][a-z]+$/ and none is in harvest.mjs's STOP set), and harvestFromDigest sorts by count descending — as string VALUES at up to 20 per window across up to 400 windows they would become the top proposals and bury the private nouns the subcommand exists to surface.

Set `correctionObserved` as a TRI-STATE, and never let absence-of-data read as evidence. 'yes' when the next window in the same session opens with a correction; 'no' when the next window exists, is not a stub, and does not; 'unknown' when there is no next window (the flushed terminal window), when the next window is a stub, or when the session's last record is within 120 seconds of this window's last record. Only 'no' may later support a positive grade. Without this, correctionsAfter = 0 is structurally guaranteed for the LAST window of EVERY session — including the one a user leaves after a bad answer, or re-asks in a fresh session — and silence would be graded as approval.

Type the status signals. Store `statusSignals` (every deriveStatus result in the window, as today) AND `testSignals` (only those whose originating tool_use, looked up in toolUseById, is a Bash command matching detectTest() at claude-adapter.mjs:263). Measured necessity: claude-adapter.mjs:352-355 calls deriveStatus on EVERY tool_result with no tool gate, and deriveStatus's regexes are substring scans — 'I made a second pass over the config' yields pass=true, 'the assertion in that helper is stale' yields fail=true, '- [x] ✓ done' yields pass=true. A Read of a test file followed by a Read of a checklist produces a fail-then-pass sequence. Only testSignals may support a Lane A grade.

Split the SHA nominations by cause. `commitShas` holds only SHAs extracted from a tool_result whose originating tool_use command matches /\bgit\s+commit\b/; `inspectedShas` holds SHAs from log/show/rev-parse. Measured necessity: GIT_INSPECT_RE (:268) is /\bgit\s+(commit|log|show|rev-parse)\b/ and extractCommits (:300-304) harvests line-leading short SHAs from `git log --oneline` output, including months-old commits and other authors'. The flat acc.candidateCommits keeps merging BOTH exactly as today (byte-identity requirement); only the window split is new.

Attribute signals to the window the CAUSE fired in, not the window the effect landed in. toolUseById (:333) is session-scoped and never cleared, so store the open window index in its value at :388 ({ name, command, turn }) and use that turn when a tool_result arrives at :356. Otherwise a long Bash run or a backgrounded build credits its status flip and its SHA to an unrelated later instruction. Records emitted BEFORE the first boundary have `turn: null`; the tool_result handler SKIPS window attribution when it is null. No synthetic window 0 is created, so turns[0] always corresponds to a real instruction, and those signals still reach the flat arrays exactly as today.

Keep the four existing flat arrays byte-identical. steers/notes/statusSignals/redirects/candidateCommits continue to be pushed exactly as today under exactly today's caps. Windows are an ADDITIONAL projection over the same stream, never a replacement. Per-window tallies are siblings of acc.counts, never a mutation of it (test/claude-adapter.test.mjs:84 deepEquals toolSignal.counts to {Edit:1,Bash:2,Grep:1}).

Add uncapped session counters: counters = { humanTurns, correctionTurns, assistantTurns, statusSignals, candidateShas }. These are incremented OUTSIDE every `if (arr.length < MAX_*)` guard. assistantTurns cannot be derived from notes.length: both `thinking` (:370) and `text` (:372) push into the SAME acc.notes under one shared MAX_NOTES = 80. correctionTurns must be counted on an independent uncapped isCorrectionTurn() test, because the redirect guard at :346 short-circuits on the cap BEFORE the regex runs.

Capture ideas from BOTH sides with an explicit origin. In the isTurnBoundary branch, test the human instruction against IDEA_CUES; in the assistant `text` branch (:372), test the assistant's text. Push { turn, ref, origin: 'you'|'assistant', cue } — and NO free text — into acc.ideas, capped at MAX_IDEAS. A cue appearing inside a tool_result body must never produce an idea (tool_result bodies are read only for status derivation and are never stored; test/claude-adapter.test.mjs:100-107 guards this). A machine-envelope turn never produces an idea.

Emit turns/ideas/counters/truncatedAtTurn on the public entry (:494-515) and add them to privateEntry() (:457-471) as [] / [] / all-zero counters / null. The shapes must stay symmetric or test/claude-adapter.test.mjs:65-75, which iterates REQUIRED_FIELDS over EVERY entry including private ones, diverges. A private/display session can never yield a turn, idea or prompt by construction, because adaptOneSession returns at :490 before extractEntry runs at :493 — preserve that ordering.

Add the prompt sink as the SOLE new channel, and DO NOT change any return shape. `adaptOneSession(file, { config, weekStart, weekEnd, redactor, promptSink })` pushes { ref, sessionId: id, turn, text } per window opening and { ref, sessionId: id, turn, origin, cue, text } per idea, where `text` is redactor.redact()-ed then capped at MAX_PROMPT_LEN. `adaptSessions({ ..., promptSink })` threads it through and STILL RETURNS THE ENTRIES ARRAY, unchanged. The earlier '{ entries, prompts } when a sink is supplied' rule would have broken all 7 tests in test/discover.test.mjs: `adapter` is injectable (discover.mjs:92), discover assigns its result straight to `sessions` (:119) and iterates it (:126), and test/discover.test.mjs:34's mockAdapter returns a BARE ARRAY — destructuring `{entries}` off an array yields undefined and 'sessions is not iterable'. With a sink, the injectable adapter contract is untouched and mockAdapter needs field additions only. `sessionId` in a sink row is the entry's shortId (claude-adapter.mjs:438-444), the same value the draft calls `id` — name that equivalence in a code comment, because the two names for one value are the single most likely source of a resolution bug downstream.

In lib/discover.mjs, ensure BOTH sidecar gitignore entries BEFORE writing either file, then write the draft (:156), then write honestweek.prompts.json sourced from the sink — NEVER from the `redacted` object at :155 and never placed inside the object passed to deepRedact. Parameterize ensureDraftGitignored (:53-70) or copy harvest.mjs:105-113: idempotent append to the USER's cwd/.gitignore plus the `git ls-files` already-tracked warning. Print COUNTS only in the summary at :160 — prompts, ideas, and any MAX_PROMPT_LEN / MAX_SIDECAR_BYTES cap hits — never a sample prompt or idea string.

Extend lib/init.mjs and the repo's own .gitignore. init.mjs:21 hardcodes DRAFT_SIDECAR and init.mjs:150 calls ensureGitignore for that one entry; the committed .gitignore lists honestweek.draft.json, honestweek.items.json and honestweek.config.json only. Add 'honestweek.prompts.json' AND 'honestweek.harvest.json' (a pre-existing gap, fixed while here) to both, so a user who runs `init` and inspects .gitignore sees the prompts entry before discover has ever created the file.

In lib/harvest.mjs, read honestweek.prompts.json as a SECOND input alongside the draft when it exists, and EXPORT the currently module-private `excludeSet(config)` (harvest.mjs:74-84) for reuse by validate and build in Phase 2. Requirement 1 removed the highest-leak-density prose from the draft, so without the second input the denylist-proposal loop stops covering it. Absent sidecar: behaviour unchanged.

In lib/handoffs.mjs, add next-steps extraction. Add MAX_NEXT_STEPS = 20 beside :18-21. Add NEXT_HEADING_RE = /^#{1,6}\s.*(next step|open question|follow[- ]?up|not done|carried forward|todo)/i beside REVERSAL_HEADING_RE (:30). Do NOT add a free-floating NEXT_LINE_RE twin of REVERSAL_LINE_RE (:31): the reversal line rule fires on any line anywhere in the document, which is tolerable for a strong keyword like 'reverted' but would make a next-steps rule swallow ordinary prose. Set BOTH section flags from the SAME `if (HEADING_RE.test(line))` block at :85, because that single assignment is also the reset — setting the new flag anywhere else leaves inReversalSection stale-true under a '## Next steps' heading and next-steps bullets land in reversals[], corrupting the exact signal Lane B uses to close ideas. PRECEDENCE RULE (nothing decides this today): a line matching both is a reversal ONLY; it is excluded from nextSteps.

Carry nextSteps through discoverHandoffs. Destructure it at :136, redact it per-field at :144 like reversals, and — critically — add it to the emptiness guard at :137. Today `if (claims.length === 0 && reversals.length === 0 && commits.length === 0) continue;` DROPS any handoff whose only content is a next-steps section, which is exactly the content this phase and #52 item 4 want. Without this the extractor's own unit tests pass while the field never reaches the draft.

Update the guards that would otherwise silently stop guarding: test/claude-adapter.test.mjs:40 REQUIRED_FIELDS gains 'turns','ideas','counters' (it uses `f in e`, so it is additive-tolerant and guards nothing new until updated); test/discover.test.mjs:34 mockAdapter gains the same ENTRY fields while keeping its bare-array RETURN (the real adapter never runs in that file, so this is the corpus's main drift hazard); test/handoffs.test.mjs:19 destructures exactly {claims,reversals,commits} and its title says 'only', so it must be edited, not merely supplemented.

Docs, in the same PR. README.md '## Sidecars' table (test/docs.test.mjs:96-100 asserts on it) gains a honestweek.prompts.json row marked gitignored, and a honestweek.harvest.json row. README.md:83 and SKILL.md:25 BOTH enumerate the handoff yield as 'tagged claims, reversals, and cited SHAs' and test/docs.test.mjs:122 asserts the two files do not contradict — both must change together. SKILL.md:25's draft-shape sentence gains turns/ideas. Correct the pre-existing drift you are touching anyway: README.md:246 and SKILL.md:31 both omit `page` (and SKILL.md:31 also omits `site`) from the output.mode enumeration, while lib/config.mjs:29 has all six.
acceptanceCriteria: `node --test` passes with zero failures from the repo root, and the pre-existing count of 371 passing tests does not decrease.

GOLDEN OUTPUT, HERMETIC: test/golden-output.test.mjs sets CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR to test/fixtures/claude-projects, passes a fixed `now` into runBuild, and points config.repos at an in-test throwaway git repo; under those three it builds every mode (post, changelog, digest, report, page, site) and asserts byte-identity against golden files committed in this PR. The same harness is asserted to produce identical bytes on two consecutive runs.

DRAFT SUPERSET: for the committed fixture corpus, every pre-existing draft key is assert.deepEqual to its pre-change value — sessions[].steers, .assistantNotes, .toolSignal, .statusSignals, .redirects, .candidateCommits, and handoffs[].claims/.reversals/.candidateCommits. Only new keys differ.

DRAFT DETERMINISM: test/discover.test.mjs:125 (running discover twice yields a byte-identical draft) still passes with turns/ideas/counters present. This fails if any Set or Map iteration order reaches serialization.

ADAPTER RETURN SHAPE UNCHANGED: a test asserts `Array.isArray(await adaptSessions({...}))` both with and without a promptSink, and all 7 tests in test/discover.test.mjs pass with mockAdapter still returning a bare array.

ENTRY COUNT UNCHANGED: test/claude-adapter.test.mjs:59 still asserts an exact entry count from the existing fixture tree, proving isHumanTurn and the interactive gate were not altered. New fixtures live in NEW project dirs and the assertion is updated to the new exact number, with its title, in the same commit.

REDACTION ORDER FIX: a unit test feeds a 303-char string ending 'alice@corp-secret.example.com more' through the steers path and asserts the output contains no '@' and no 'corp-secret'. A second test asserts the measured SHIFT directly: a 358-char string with '/home/alice/notes' at offset 40 yields a 279-char steer under the old order and 281 under the new. A third asserts discover over the committed fixture corpus is byte-identical before and after the reorder, and the test name states WHY (the fixtures contain no over-length mined string).

MACHINE ENVELOPES OPEN NO WINDOW: fixtures containing a <task-notification>, a <local-command-caveat>, a <local-command-stdout>, a <system-reminder> and a <cross-session-message from=... name="..."> record each assert turns.length is unchanged by that record. Specifically: a <command-name> turn followed by <local-command-caveat> and <local-command-stdout> produces exactly ONE window, of kind 'command', and the tool results that follow are attributed to it by exact index.

TURN ATTRIBUTION: a new multi-turn featured fixture proves each signal lands in the window whose instruction preceded it — a tool_use fired in window 1 whose tool_result arrives during window 2 is attributed to window 1, asserted by exact index.

SLASH-COMMAND ARGS NEVER READ: a fixture driving work through '<command-name>run-tests</command-name><command-args>SECRETARG</command-args>' produces a window with kind === 'command', and 'SECRETARG' appears in no entry, no draft, and no sidecar row.

PRE-FIRST-WINDOW SIGNAL: a fixture session opening with an assistant record still contributes to toolSignal.counts exactly as today (assert.deepEqual on counts), turns[0] corresponds to the first real instruction, and no window carries those pre-boundary signals.

BOUND TESTS: a synthetic session with 200 human turns yields exactly MAX_STEERS = 60 emitted steers AND counters.humanTurns === 200 AND turns.length === 200. A synthetic session with 500 turns yields turns.length === 400, entry.truncatedAtTurn === 400, and every past-cap window present as `{ index, stub: true, complete: false }` — asserted by key set, not by absence.

COMPLETE-FLAG ENUMERATION: a synthetic session that trips MAX_TOOLS_PER_TURN in one window asserts that window has complete === false and its neighbours have complete === true. A synthetic session with 100 human turns (past MAX_STEERS = 60) asserts EVERY non-stub window still has complete === true, proving the flat-array caps do not touch the flag. A synthetic session with 40 correction turns asserts counters.correctionTurns === 40 while redirects.length === 30, and that no window's complete flag changed as a result.

CORRECTION TRI-STATE: the flushed terminal window of every fixture session carries correctionObserved === 'unknown'; a window whose successor opens with a correction carries 'yes'; a window whose successor exists and does not carries 'no'; a window whose successor is a stub carries 'unknown'.

TYPED SIGNALS: a fixture whose only status signal comes from a Read tool_result containing the word 'pass' asserts statusSignals has one entry and testSignals is EMPTY. A fixture with a Bash `npm test` result asserts the signal appears in both.

SHA CAUSE SPLIT: a fixture window whose only git activity is `git log --oneline` asserts commitShas is empty and inspectedShas is non-empty; a `git commit` window asserts the reverse. The flat entry.candidateCommits is assert.deepEqual to its pre-change value in both.

SHAPEKEY FLOOR: a window whose instruction is 'continue' yields shapeKey === null; one reading 'ok do it' yields null; one with six or more content words yields an 8-hex string. A synthetic corpus repeating 'continue' across three sessions yields zero shapeKey groups.

NO PROSE IN THE DRAFT (the structural control, and the assertion the promptVerbatim probe would have failed): a scan asserts every turns[] and ideas[] object has exactly the specified key set and every string value is either a member of a closed vocabulary (a cue, 'prose'|'command', 'you'|'assistant', a tool name, a status token) or matches /^[0-9a-f]{8}$/.

TOOLSUSED IS AN OBJECT: a test asserts typeof turns[i].toolsUsed === 'object' && !Array.isArray(...), and that harvestFromDigest over a turns-bearing draft proposes none of 'Edit','Bash','Grep','Read','Write','Glob','Task'.

SIDECAR: running discover on the fixture corpus creates honestweek.prompts.json, and cwd/.gitignore already contains both the prompts and harvest entries BEFORE either file is written (asserted by an io-order spy or by an fs mtime comparison). Running discover twice adds one line each. The already-tracked warning path fires when `git ls-files` reports the file tracked. discover's stdout contains counts and no prompt text.

INIT GITIGNORES BOTH SIDECARS: running `honestweek init` alone, with no discover run, leaves cwd/.gitignore containing 'honestweek.prompts.json' and 'honestweek.harvest.json'. The repo's own committed .gitignore contains both.
SIDECAR BOUNDS: a synthetic session with a 50,000-character human turn yields a sidecar `text` of exactly MAX_PROMPT_LEN characters, and discover's stdout reports the cap hit as a count.

NEGATIVE CONTROL, Phase-1 half (restated to what is true): a new fixture human turn contains an UNCONFIGURED private noun. The noun appears in honestweek.prompts.json; appears in NO turns[] and NO ideas[] object in honestweek.draft.json; and appears in NO built artifact in any mode. The test explicitly does NOT assert whole-file absence from the draft, and carries a comment stating that steers[] legitimately holds that turn verbatim-truncated today. No shapeKey and no ref value appears in any built artifact.

IDEA NEGATIVE CONTROLS: an 'idea:' string inside a tool_result body produces no idea; a mid-sentence 'that's a good idea' produces no idea (the anchored regex); a line-leading 'Idea: ...' in an assistant text block produces an idea with origin === 'assistant'; the same in a human turn produces origin === 'you'; the word 'later' alone produces no idea.

HANDOFF: extractHandoff returns {claims, reversals, nextSteps, commits}; a handoff whose ONLY content is a '## Next steps' section produces a draft entry (proving the :137 guard was updated); a bullet under '## Next steps' reading 'revisit the reverted retry queue' appears in reversals[] and NOT in nextSteps[]; a '## Next steps' heading following a '## Reversals' heading resets inReversalSection to false; a 30-bullet next-steps section yields exactly MAX_NEXT_STEPS = 20 entries.

PRIVATE SYMMETRY: every private entry carries turns === [], ideas === [], counters with all-zero values and truncatedAtTurn === null; REQUIRED_FIELDS includes the new names and the schema test passes over private and public entries alike.
CLEAN-ROOM: a new test scans lib/lanes.mjs against test/site-cleanroom.test.mjs's FORBIDDEN token list (case-insensitive substring) and passes.
DOCS: test/docs.test.mjs and test/skill.test.mjs pass, including the subcommand-set assertion (no new subcommand is introduced by this phase) and the sidecar-table assertion.
testPlan: New test/lanes.test.mjs: unit-test shapeKeyFor (same first 6 content words -> same key; differing 7th -> same key; digit-normalization; null below the 6-content-word floor; null for a filler-only turn), refFor stability across two runs and its origin sensitivity (same session/turn/text with different origin -> different ref), normalizePhrase, IDEA_CUES matching plus non-matching controls (mid-sentence 'idea', bare 'later'), isMachineEnvelope over one fixture per censused tag class, and sharesRun (containment at 5 and 6 words true; 8-word overlap true; 7-word overlap in a long string true; an unrelated paraphrase false; punctuation- and case-insensitive).

New test/golden-output.test.mjs: hermetic harness (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR pinned to the fixture tree, fixed `now`, in-test throwaway git repo) building all six modes into a temp dir and comparing byte-for-byte against test/fixtures/golden/. Reused unchanged by Phases 2 and 3.

risks: Changing isHumanTurn instead of adding isTurnBoundary would move the digest's session SET and break the exact-count assertion at test/claude-adapter.test.mjs:59 while leaving lib/site/sessions.mjs's deliberately different isInteractiveFirstPrompt classifier untouched — a silent divergence between the two readers (documented as intentional at sessions.mjs:118-133).

The machine-envelope classifier is a denylist plus a catch-all. A future Claude Code release inventing a new envelope tag with free prose outside its blocks would open a spurious window. The catch-all (unknown well-formed tag-only content is machine) is the fail-closed direction, but it is a heuristic over an interface honestweek does not control, and the census that grounds it (300 local session files) is one machine's corpus.
Forgetting to flush the final open window before `return acc` (claude-adapter.mjs:381) drops the last, usually most productive, window of EVERY session. No existing test would catch it.

Holding per-window toolsUsed as a Set, or windows as a Map keyed by turn index, silently serializes to {} — deepRedact and JSON.stringify both do this, so it would not even show as corruption in a draft diff.

The handoffs.mjs:137 emptiness-guard change is a real behaviour delta for existing users, not a pure addition. If it is omitted the extractor's unit tests pass and the field never reaches the draft; if it is included without being written up, users see new handoff entries appear unexplained.

Redact-before-truncate changes draft bytes for ANY over-length mined string carrying a redactable token before the cut — common on a real corpus, absent from the fixtures. The fixture byte-identity gate therefore proves less than it appears to, which is why the direct shift measurement and the PR-body note are both required rather than optional.
Slash-command windows read <command-name> only. If <command-args> is ever read, hashed or written to the sidecar, arbitrary private argument text enters a new surface.

The prompts sidecar must be built from the sink, never from discover.mjs:155's `redacted` object and never placed inside the object handed to deepRedact — the second would give it published shape, the first would silently drop the untruncated-then-capped form.

MAX_PROMPT_LEN = 4000 is a judgement call, not a measurement. It is large enough that sharesRun's containment and n-gram tests behave identically to an uncapped corpus for any realistic authored name, but a pathological instruction whose only copied span sits past character 4000 would evade the copy gate. Stated rather than hidden; revisit if a real corpus shows instructions routinely exceeding it.

The gitignore-before-write ordering closes the accidental-tracking window but does not close it retroactively: a user who already ran a pre-Phase-1 discover has no prompts file, so there is nothing to un-track. Users who somehow have one are covered by the existing `git ls-files` warning, which is a warning and not a refusal.
